name: 3D Gaze Point Selection
summary: Select objects at different depths on a stereo display by gaze alone: the eye tracker estimates both where you look and how far, from the distance between your two pupils.
howItWorks: Gaze direction is estimated from the pupil and two corneal glints of one eye; gaze depth from the pupil-centre distance (PCD) between both eyes, which grows as the eyes converge less on farther points, after a short per-user calibration. The intersection of the gaze direction with the estimated depth plane gives a 3D gaze point; looking at an object for about 1 s selects it. An ultrasonic sensor compensates small head movements. Built with a single camera and IR LEDs for a parallax-barrier autostereoscopic display, distinguishing four depth levels (0.63–2.6 m); in a dart-and-arrow demo, gaze picked the arrow and then a point on the dart. Selection accuracy within 1 s was at least 93% over 9 regions x 4 depths (3 users).

relationships.note: Adds gaze depth from binocular vergence to gaze selection.
